title: Addressing fusiform gyrus dysfunction in schizophrenia, theory of mind, and implications for antipsychotics’ response and resistance: A systematic review and critical appraisal
title_zh: 解码精神分裂症中梭状回功能失调、心智理论及其对抗精神病药物反应与耐药性的影响：系统综述与批判性评估
abstract: BACKGROUND: The Fusiform Gyrus (FG), a brain region relevant for the interaction between cognitive processes and emotional behavior, especially emotion recognition and interpretation of social cues, has been linked to the pathophysiology of schizophrenia conceptualized as a disorder of aberrant synaptic function and brain connectivity as well as characterized by disruptions in thought processes, perceptions, emotional responsiveness, and Theory of Mind (ToM). Disrupted FG connectivity has been reported in schizophrenia; however, no systematic review has addressed this issue in a comprehensive and critical manner. METHODS: We conducted a systematic review of PubMed, Embase, and Scopus from database inception to February 2026 following PRISMA guidelines. We included peer-reviewed neuroimaging studies using functional magnetic resonance imaging to assess functional connectivity or task-related activation of the FG in patients with schizophrenia compared with healthy controls. RESULTS: We identified 2765 articles from different sources. After duplicate removal, 959 articles were screened at the title-abstract level, 269 articles were reviewed for full-texts, and 86 eligible articles were included. Across fMRI studies, the FG emerged as a central node of dysconnectivity. Drug-naïve patients showed heterogeneous FG alterations, with increased local activity and network centrality reported in some studies and reduced interhemispheric and functional connectivity in others, alongside reduced FG activation on visual, affective, and sensory tasks reported more broadly across schizophrenia samples. First-episode psychosis patients were characterized by FG hypoconnectivity associated with negative symptoms and socio-cognitive impairment. Treatment-responsive patients demonstrated partial normalization or modulation of fusiform connectivity and network centrality following antipsychotic treatment. In contrast, treatment-resistant schizophrenia patients showed persistent hypoactivation and reduced connectivity, correlating with cognitive deficits and negative symptoms. CONCLUSIONS: The FG appears to function as a dynamic, state-sensitive hub underlying perceptual, emotional, and cognitive disturbances in schizophrenia, in line with impaired ToM.
abstract_zh: 背景：梭状回（FG）是与认知过程与情绪行为交互相关的脑区，尤其在情绪识别和社会线索解释中发挥作用。它已被关联到精神分裂症的病理生理学，后者被概念化为突触功能异常和脑网络连接失调的疾病，并表现为思维过程、知觉、情绪反应和心智理论（ToM）的中断。已有研究报告精神分裂症患者的FG连接受损，但尚无系统综述以全面且批判的方式探讨此问题。方法：我们依据PRISMA指南，对PubMed、Embase和Scopus自数据库创建至2026年2月的文献进行系统综述。纳入使用功能磁共振成像（fMRI）评估精神分裂症患者与健康对照组FG功能连接或任务相关激活的同行评议神经影像学研究。结果：我们共检索到2765篇文章，去重后筛选959篇进行标题-摘要评估，269篇进入全文评估，最终纳入86篇符合条件的研究。跨fMRI研究显示，FG成为失调连接的核心节点。无药物治疗的患者表现出FG改变的异质性，有研究报告局部活动和网络中心性增加，亦有研究报告双侧脑半球间及功能连接下降，且在视觉、情感和感官任务中FG激活普遍降低。首次发作精神病患者的FG低连接与负性症状及社会认知障碍相关。对药物有反应的患者在抗精神病治疗后显示FG连接和网络中心性部分恢复或调节。相反，治疗耐药精神分裂症患者则表现出持续的低激活和连接下降，且与认知缺陷和负性症状相关。结论：FG似乎作为一个动态、状态敏感的枢纽，支撑精神分裂症中的感知、情绪和认知障碍，符合ToM受损的理论。
